mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in the federal funds rate compresses equity valuations through higher discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as monetary policy tightens.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods with consecutive 3-month FEDFUNDS increases, or Rank IC < 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate falling below 4.0% signals a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE < 4.0%, or average return in triggered periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts and retail sales indicates robust consumer demand, increasing corporate revenue expectations and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS show specified MoM growth, or interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 2.5%) reduce liquidity and increase borrowing costs, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.5%, or average return in tightening cycles is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls indicates labor market strength that supports consumer spending and corporate profits, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with consecutive 3-month PAYEMS increases, or Rank IC < 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts falling below 1200 thousand units signals weak residential demand that reduces economic growth expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when HOUST < 1200, or average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in industrial production and GDP growth indicates robust supply chain activity and economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when both INDPRO and GDPC1 exceed thresholds, or interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Supply chain disruption events (INDPRO < 105) reduce industrial output and corporate production capacity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO < 105, or average return in disruption periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).
